transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-11
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood Solutions), Dana Lopez (CISO, Archon), Matt Rivera (Head of Platform), Priya Singh (SRE), Omar Khalid (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking time. quick intros?
[00:08] Dana Lopez: Dana, CISO at Archon, we'll be responsible for security sign-off, hi.
[00:12] Matt Rivera: Matt, head of platform, we'll run the pilot and own infra.
[00:17] Ethan Park: Ethan here, I'm the SE, I'll go over technical posture and integration bits.
[00:22] Maya Chen: great, agenda is security posture, SOC2/ISO, SSO and RBAC, encryption/KMS, audit logs and retention, plus deployment options.
[00:35] Dana Lopez: sounds good. to frame, Archon processes PHI and we need controls aligned with HIPAA, plus our security team requires SOC2 type 2 and ISO27001 before prod. also thinking about data residency in our AWS us-east-2 region.
[00:54] Ethan Park: totally understood. high level: Redwood offers hosted (shared), Dedicated reserved GPU pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). for PHI we typically see customers choose Dedicated or Private; hosted can work with strict contracts but we understand it's less common for PHI.
[01:18] Priya Singh: quick q, what does private mean operationally? is the control plane still managed by Redwood or fully customer-run?
[01:28] Jordan Li: for Private we provide a customer-controlled VPC option where the control plane can be either customer-managed or a private control plane managed under a dedicated contract. there are versions - fully air-gapped on-prem is available for the largest customers. sorry that was a mouthful, but yes you get network isolation and optional control plane custody.
[01:48] Dana Lopez: ok, and KMS? we require keys that we control and HSM-backed if possible.
[01:55] Ethan Park: we integrate with customer KMS including AWS KMS and external HSMs. customers can bring keys (BYOK) and we support envelope encryption patterns. there's an audit trail whenever keys are used for model payload crypto.
[02:15] Matt Rivera: nice, does that extend to model artifacts and cached KV? we can't have unencrypted caches holding PHI.
[02:25] Ethan Park: good question - KV cache and any on-disk artifacts in Dedicated/Private are encrypted at rest with your keys. for hosted we have encryption at rest but BYOK is available on Dedicated and Private and recommended for PHI workloads.
[02:42] [00:03:00] Maya Chen: on compliance attestations, we can share SOC2 Type 2 reports and ISO27001 certificates, plus latest penetration test summary. I'll follow up with the pack.
[03:02] Dana Lopez: what about SSO and provisioning? we use Okta and want SAML for the console and SCIM for provisioning service accounts.
[03:12] Ethan Park: Redwood supports SAML SSO (Okta, Azure AD) and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is configurable - you can create roles, map SAML groups to roles, and enforce least privilege. we also have token types for service-to-service calls and fine-grained route/model permissions in the console and API.
[03:34] Priya Singh: how do audit logs work? retention and access? we need immutable logs for 12 months and SOC-level log export.
[03:44] Jordan Li: audit logs include user activity, API calls, model rollouts, key rotations. Logs can be streamed to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via secure connectors or pulled via API. retention policies are configurable; for Dedicated/Private we can meet 12+ months and export as needed.
[04:04] Dana Lopez: we also want proof of data lineage - if a model generated output from PHI prompts, we need to trace request ID and where data was stored.
[04:14] Ethan Park: every request has an ID and we persist metadata about route/model version, timestamps, and which cache keys were hit. we can surface those in logs and link to auditing systems; for Private deployments you can choose to store only hashed metadata if you want minimal persistence.
[04:34] [00:06:00] Matt Rivera: latency and cost tradeoffs: our product needs sub-300ms p50 for short prompts, but we also run large batches overnight. how do you guarantee latency on Dedicated?
[04:46] Ethan Park: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; you can reserve capacity for p50 SLOs. we also have autoscale and burst options, and kernel selection plus batching optimizations. we'll share performance profiles per model. note that for strict latency SLOs private on-prem might be best but Dedicated often satisfies with the right commit.
[05:12] Dana Lopez: are there third-party pen tests or bug bounty programs? we need independent validation.
[05:20] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood runs annual third-party pen tests and has a vulnerability disclosure program; we can share summaries and scope documents.
[05:30] Omar Khalid: procurement question - if we go Dedicated how does SLA and termination look? we have legal that needs to review data handling terms.
[05:40] Jordan Li: SLA terms are in the enterprise contract; Dedicated has uptime and latency targets and data handling addenda. for termination we have data deletion and transit proofs; we provide certificates of deletion and audit logs showing final state. we'll liaison legal if needed.
[05:59] [00:12:00] Dana Lopez: incident response - what's your process and RTO/RPO guarantees?
[06:05] Ethan Park: we have an incident response playbook, on-call and priorities; for Dedicated customers we offer faster escalation and runbooks with joint runbooks if desired. RTO/RPO depends on deployment and config, but we'll provide specifics in the security pack.
[06:20] Priya Singh: can we run a pilot in our staging VPC that mimics prod? we want to test with redacted PHI.
[06:27] Maya Chen: absolutely - pilots are usually Dedicated trial capacity or Private staging. we can provision a Dedicated pool scoped to your VPC and run benchmarks.
[06:36] Matt Rivera: what about data retention and the ability to purge datasets, including caches and logs?
[06:42] Ethan Park: retention is configurable by route. caches can be TTL'd and purged, and logs can be archived or deleted per policy. for PHI we recommend configurations that avoid persisting raw prompts or use token-level redaction and prefix-only caching.
[07:00] Dana Lopez: encryption in transit, do you support mTLS to the runtime?
[07:05] Jordan Li: yes TLS 1.2/1.3 by default, and mTLS is supported for Private deployments and can be configured for Dedicated.
[07:15] [00:18:00] Priya Singh: curious about key rotation: can we rotate keys without downtime and is there support for key versioning?
[07:22] Ethan Park: yes, envelope encryption supports key versioning and rotation; we support staged rotation with dual-key decrypt for brief overlap to avoid downtime. logs capture rotation events.
[07:36] Dana Lopez: any limitations on third-party integrations for SIEM or identity providers?
[07:42] Maya Chen: we support common SIEMs and IdPs; if you have a custom provider we can typically build a connector or use generic syslog/HTTPS forwarding.
[07:56] Matt Rivera: regarding model governance, do you provide model whitelisting and rollback? if a model regresses we need easy rollback.
[08:04] Ethan Park: yes, model versioning, canary rollouts, automatic fallback policies to a safe model variant, and manual rollback are all supported. we also have eval hooks to monitor quality regressions against prompt sets.
[08:24] [00:24:00] Dana Lopez: one risk is data exfiltration from generated outputs - any mitigation?
[08:30] Jordan Li: we provide content filters, allowlist/denylist controls, and output redaction at route level. for high-risk workloads we recommend Private deployments and additional monitoring on outputs.
[08:46] Priya Singh: for the pilot, what telemetry will you need from us? we'll probably provide sample prompts and traffic pattern docs.
[08:52] Ethan Park: ideally sample request set, typical concurrency, average sequence lengths, and any prompts containing PII/PHI to validate filters. also retention policy for logs and expected SLO targets.
[09:08] Maya Chen: recap - we'll send SOC2/ISO/pen-test, security pack, pilot/pricing options. Ethan will schedule infra deep-dive and benchmark. Archon will send sample workloads and retention requirements.
[09:22] Dana Lopez: sounds good. final Q: can we get a redacted pen test report or is it fully redacted? legal would want at least scope and high-level findings.
[09:30] Maya Chen: we can provide an executive summary and redacted findings, full report under NDA if required.
[09:37] Omar Khalid: ok procurement will start intake once we have the security pack and pilot pricings.
[09:42] [00:30:00] Maya Chen: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and schedule. any other questions?
[09:48] Matt Rivera: no, thanks.
[09:50] Priya Singh: thanks all.
[09:52] Dana Lopez: thanks, bye.

End transcript.
